issues.concern: The headword '博士' is not inherently formal. While it can be used in formal contexts, it's also commonly used in neutral or even informal settings (e.g., '恐竜博士'). The 'formal' tag is misleading for an intermediate learner.

The translation 'the professor' for '博士' in this context is misleading. While 'professor' can be a translation for 博士, in this specific sentence, 'expert' or 'know-it-all' would be more appropriate given the preceding clause '何でも知っているので' (since he knows everything). 'The professor' implies an academic title, which isn't necessarily the case here.
issues.suggestion: Since he knows everything, everyone calls him 'the expert' (or 'the know-it-all').
